sandhi.rule: the m of the prefix sam becomes anusvāra and then the nasalised l homorganic with the following l (Pāṇini 8.3.23 mo 'nusvāraḥ; 8.4.58 anusvārasya yayi parasavarṇaḥ); the nasalised ll is ordinarily written plain ll

samasa.type: bahuvrīhi (over an inner tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa, a ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa and a karmadhāraya)
samasa.vigraha: निजः सल्लापः निजसल्लापः; निजसल्लापस्य माधुर्यम् निजसल्लापमाधुर्यम्; निजसल्लापमाधुर्येण विनिर्भर्त्सिता निजसल्लापमाधुर्यविनिर्भर्त्सिता; निजसल्लापमाधुर्यविनिर्भर्त्सिता कच्छपी यया सा निजसल्लापमाधुर्यविनिर्भर्त्सितकच्छपी
samasa.vigraha_iast: nijaḥ sallāpaḥ nijasallāpaḥ; nijasallāpasya mādhuryam nijasallāpamādhuryam; nijasallāpamādhuryeṇa vinirbhartsitā nijasallāpamādhuryavinirbhartsitā; nijasallāpamādhuryavinirbhartsitā kacchapī yayā sā nijasallāpamādhuryavinirbhartsitakacchapī
samasa.explanation: (1) nija-sallāpa 'Her own speech' (karmadhāraya). (2) …sallāpa-mādhurya 'the sweetness of that speech' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (3) The passive participle vinirbhartsitā 'rebuked, put to shame' takes the sweetness as its instrument (tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa). (4) The whole is a bahuvrīhi in the instrumental relation: 'She by whom the Kacchapī has been put to shame by the sweetness of Her own speech'. The participle takes its masculine stem inside the bahuvrīhi (puṃvadbhāva); kacchapī is the last member and keeps its feminine ī.

components.note: sam + √lap 'to speak'; the same word as saṃlāpa
vi + nir + √bharts 'to threaten, scold', past participle

components.meaning: the Kacchapī, the vīṇā of Sarasvatī
components.note: named from kacchapa 'tortoise', after the tortoise-shaped body of the instrument

names.meaning: She who puts to shame even Sarasvatī's vīṇā, the Kacchapī, by the sweetness of Her own speech
names.significance: In Saundaryalaharī 66 Sarasvatī, singing Śiva's deeds on her vīṇā, quietly wraps the instrument in its cover when the Goddess answers her, ashamed of its tone beside Her voice. Traditionally Her speech is the source of all speech, of which Sarasvatī's music is a part.

meaning_check.note: ITRANS 'veeNa of sarasvatI' put into IAST and the instrument's name, Kacchapī, given; vinirbhartsita is 'put to shame', stronger than 'excels'.

names.previous_split_issues: vinirbhartsita was glossed 'excelling/reproaching'; it is the passive participle 'rebuked, put to shame'. sallāpa was not explained (sam + lāpa).

sandhi.rule: guṇa: a + ī → e (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ), inside the lexicalised name Kāmeśa

samasa.type: bahuvrīhi (over an inner karmadhāraya, saptamī-tatpuruṣa and ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣas)
samasa.vigraha: मन्दम् स्मितम् मन्दस्मितम्; मन्दस्मितस्य प्रभा मन्दस्मितप्रभा; मन्दस्मितप्रभायाः पूरः मन्दस्मितप्रभापूरः; मन्दस्मितप्रभापूरे मज्जत् मन्दस्मितप्रभापूरमज्जत्; कामेशस्य मानसम् कामेशमानसम्; मन्दस्मितप्रभापूरमज्जत् कामेशमानसम् यस्याः सा मन्दस्मितप्रभापूरमज्जत्कामेशमानसा
samasa.vigraha_iast: mandam smitam mandasmitam; mandasmitasya prabhā mandasmitaprabhā; mandasmitaprabhāyāḥ pūraḥ mandasmitaprabhāpūraḥ; mandasmitaprabhāpūre majjat mandasmitaprabhāpūramajjat; kāmeśasya mānasam kāmeśamānasam; mandasmitaprabhāpūramajjat kāmeśamānasam yasyāḥ sā mandasmitaprabhāpūramajjatkāmeśamānasā
samasa.explanation: (1) manda-smita 'a gentle smile' (karmadhāraya). (2) …smita-prabhā 'its radiance' and …prabhā-pūra 'the flood of that radiance' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣas). (3) The present participle majjat 'sinking, being immersed' is intransitive and takes the flood in the locative (saptamī-tatpuruṣa): 'sinking in that flood'. (4) It qualifies kāmeśa-mānasa 'the mind of Kāmeśa' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa inside, karmadhāraya with the participle). (5) The whole is a bahuvrīhi: 'She in the flood of whose gentle smile's radiance Kāmeśa's mind is immersed'; mānasa takes the feminine -ā. She does not plunge His mind; it sinks of itself.

components.note: √smi 'to smile', past participle used as a noun

components.meaning: Kāmeśa, Lord of desire: Śiva as Her consort

components.note: mānasa, with the feminine -ā of the bahuvrīhi

names.meaning: She in the flood of whose gentle smile's radiance the mind of Kāmeśa is immersed
names.significance: Traditionally even Kāmeśvara, Śiva who is ever self-possessed, is absorbed in Her smile; the smile is read as the bliss in which consciousness delights in itself.

meaning_check.note: The previous wording made Her the agent ('She who submerges'); in the compound the mind sinks (majjat is intransitive) in the flood of Her smile's radiance. 'KAmesha' put into IAST.

names.previous_split_issues: prabhāpūra was left as one row (prabhā + pūra); majjat was glossed 'immersing' (transitive) — it is 'sinking, being immersed'.

samasa.type: tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa (over inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa, karmadhāraya, bahuvrīhi and nañ-tatpuruṣa)
samasa.vigraha: न आकलितम् अनाकलितम्; अनाकलितम् सादृश्यम् यस्य तत् अनाकलितसादृश्यम्; अनाकलितसादृश्यम् चिबुकम् अनाकलितसादृश्यचिबुकम्; अनाकलितसादृश्यचिबुकस्य श्रीः अनाकलितसादृश्यचिबुकश्रीः; तया विराजिता अनाकलितसादृश्यचिबुकश्रीविराजिता
samasa.vigraha_iast: na ākalitam anākalitam; anākalitam sādṛśyam yasya tat anākalitasādṛśyam; anākalitasādṛśyam cibukam anākalitasādṛśyacibukam; anākalitasādṛśyacibukasya śrīḥ anākalitasādṛśyacibukaśrīḥ; tayā virājitā anākalitasādṛśyacibukaśrīvirājitā
samasa.explanation: (1) an-ākalita 'not conceived, never found' (nañ-tatpuruṣa; the negative na appears as an- before a vowel, a morphological replacement, Pāṇini 6.3.73–74). (2) anākalita-sādṛśya 'whose likeness has never been conceived' (bahuvrīhi), qualifying cibuka 'chin' (karmadhāraya). (3) …cibuka-śrī 'the beauty of that chin' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (4) The participle virājitā 'shining, made splendid' is the head and takes the beauty in the instrumental. Incomparability is not a separate word: it comes from 'whose likeness was never conceived'.

components.note: the negative na, as an- before a vowel

names.meaning: She who shines with the beauty of a chin for which no likeness can be conceived
names.significance: Saundaryalaharī 67 ends its verse on the chin by asking how it can be described, since it has no comparison (aupamya-rahita); here too the poet finds nothing to set beside it.

meaning_check.note: The typo 'camporison' removed; the name's head, virājitā 'shining with the beauty (śrī) of the chin', was missing.

names.previous_split_issues: anākalita was glossed 'incomparable'; it means 'not conceived, never found' — incomparability arises only with sādṛśya 'likeness'. śrī was glossed 'sacred/auspicious'; here it is the chin's beauty.

sandhi.rule: guṇa: a + ī → e (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ), inside the lexicalised name Kāmeśa

samasa.type: bahuvrīhi (over inner tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣas and karmadhārayas)
samasa.vigraha: कामेशेन बद्धम् कामेशबद्धम्; माङ्गल्यम् सूत्रम् माङ्गल्यसूत्रम्; कामेशबद्धम् माङ्गल्यसूत्रम् कामेशबद्धमाङ्गल्यसूत्रम्; कामेशबद्धमाङ्गल्यसूत्रेण शोभिता कामेशबद्धमाङ्गल्यसूत्रशोभिता; कामेशबद्धमाङ्गल्यसूत्रशोभिता कन्धरा यस्याः सा कामेशबद्धमाङ्गल्यसूत्रशोभितकन्धरा
samasa.vigraha_iast: kāmeśena baddham kāmeśabaddham; māṅgalyam sūtram māṅgalyasūtram; kāmeśabaddham māṅgalyasūtram kāmeśabaddhamāṅgalyasūtram; kāmeśabaddhamāṅgalyasūtreṇa śobhitā kāmeśabaddhamāṅgalyasūtraśobhitā; kāmeśabaddhamāṅgalyasūtraśobhitā kandharā yasyāḥ sā kāmeśabaddhamāṅgalyasūtraśobhitakandharā
samasa.explanation: (1) kāmeśa-baddha 'tied by Kāmeśa' (tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa: agent in the instrumental with a past participle). (2) māṅgalya-sūtra 'the auspicious thread', the marriage thread (karmadhāraya), qualified by (1). (3) śobhitā 'adorned' takes that thread in the instrumental (tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa). (4) The whole is a bahuvrīhi: 'She whose neck is adorned with …'; śobhitā takes its masculine stem inside the bahuvrīhi (puṃvadbhāva), and kandharā 'neck' ends the name.

names.meaning: She whose neck is adorned with the marriage thread tied by Kāmeśa
names.significance: The māṅgalyasūtra is the emblem of the wedded wife. Traditionally it marks the eternal union of Kāmeśvara and Kāmeśvarī, Śiva and Śakti, who are never apart.

meaning_check.note: 'KAmesha' put into IAST.

sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)
savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

samasa.type: tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa (over inner karmadhārayas, a tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa and a dvandva)
samasa.vigraha: अङ्गदानि च केयूराणि च अङ्गदकेयूराणि; कनकमयानि अङ्गदकेयूराणि कनकाङ्गदकेयूराणि; कनकाङ्गदकेयूरैः कमनीयाः कनकाङ्गदकेयूरकमनीयाः; कनकाङ्गदकेयूरकमनीयाः भुजाः कनकाङ्गदकेयूरकमनीयभुजाः; तैः अन्विता कनकाङ्गदकेयूरकमनीयभुजान्विता
samasa.vigraha_iast: aṅgadāni ca keyūrāṇi ca aṅgadakeyūrāṇi; kanakamayāni aṅgadakeyūrāṇi kanakāṅgadakeyūrāṇi; kanakāṅgadakeyūraiḥ kamanīyāḥ kanakāṅgadakeyūrakamanīyāḥ; kanakāṅgadakeyūrakamanīyāḥ bhujāḥ kanakāṅgadakeyūrakamanīyabhujāḥ; taiḥ anvitā kanakāṅgadakeyūrakamanīyabhujānvitā
samasa.explanation: (1) aṅgada and keyūra, two kinds of upper-arm ornament, form a dvandva. (2) kanaka 'gold' qualifies them with the middle word 'made of' understood (karmadhāraya). Since aṅgada stands next to kanaka, one may also take kanaka with aṅgada alone ('golden aṅgadas and keyūras'); the sense is the same. (3) kamanīya 'lovely' takes the ornaments in the instrumental (tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa) and (4) qualifies bhuja 'arm' (karmadhāraya). (5) The participle anvitā 'endowed with' is the head and takes the arms in the instrumental.

components.meaning: aṅgada, an armlet worn on the upper arm

names.meaning: She who is endowed with arms made lovely by golden armlets (aṅgada and keyūra)
names.significance: Part of the head-to-foot description of Her form; the arms that hold the four emblems (names 8–11) are adorned with gold.

meaning_check.note: Both kinds of armlet are named, and the head of the compound, anvitā 'endowed with (such arms)', is kept.

names.previous_split_issues: kanakāṅgada and bhujānvitā were each left as one row (kanaka + aṅgada; bhuja + anvitā).

sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)
yaṇ: u becomes v before a dissimilar vowel (Pāṇini 6.1.77 iko yaṇ aci), at the junction of the prefix anu with ita

samasa.type: tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa (over an itaretara-dvandva of three members, with inner karmadhārayas)
samasa.vigraha: रत्नखचितम् ग्रैवेयम् रत्नग्रैवेयम्; लोलानि मुक्ताफलानि लोलमुक्ताफलानि; रत्नग्रैवेयम् च चिन्ताकम् च लोलमुक्ताफलानि च रत्नग्रैवेयचिन्ताकलोलमुक्ताफलानि; तैः अन्विता रत्नग्रैवेयचिन्ताकलोलमुक्ताफलान्विता
samasa.vigraha_iast: ratnakhacitam graiveyam ratnagraiveyam; lolāni muktāphalāni lolamuktāphalāni; ratnagraiveyam ca cintākam ca lolamuktāphalāni ca ratnagraiveyacintākalolamuktāphalāni; taiḥ anvitā ratnagraiveyacintākalolamuktāphalānvitā
samasa.explanation: (1) ratna-graiveya 'a necklace set with gems' (karmadhāraya with the middle word 'set with' dropped). (2) lola-muktāphala 'swaying pearls' (karmadhāraya). (3) These and cintāka, a neck ornament, are joined as an itaretara-dvandva: 'the jewelled necklace, the cintāka and the swaying pearls'. (4) The participle anvitā 'endowed with, wearing' is the head and takes them in the instrumental. muktāphala 'pearl' is one word (lit. 'pearl-fruit'); its phala belongs to it, not to anvitā.

components.meaning: cintāka, a neck ornament (collar or pendant)
components.note: a rare word known from this name and its commentators; a close-fitting necklace of this name is still worn in western and southern India

names.meaning: She who is adorned with a jewelled necklace, a cintāka and swaying pearls
names.significance: Another stage of the description of Her form, at the neck and breast; the ornaments of the Goddess are part of Her worship (bhūṣaṇa), offered to Her in pūjā.

meaning_check.note: 'neck' is not in the name and lola 'swaying' was not translated; the name lists three ornaments joined by anvitā, rather than a necklace with a locket made of pearl.

names.previous_split_issues: phalānvitā was glossed 'endowed with fruits': phala belongs to muktāphala 'pearl', and anvitā is a separate member (muktāphala + anvitā).
names.uncertain: The exact form of the cintāka is not certain: it is taken as a gold collar-necklace or as the pendant (locket) of the jewelled necklace. On the second reading the analysis is 'the jewelled necklace with its pendant, and swaying pearls'.

sandhi.rule: guṇa: a + ī → e (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ), inside the lexicalised name Kāmeśvara

samasa.type: bahuvrīhi (over inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣas and karmadhārayas)
samasa.vigraha: कामेश्वरस्य प्रेम कामेश्वरप्रेम; रत्नम् मणिः रत्नमणिः; कामेश्वरप्रेम एव रत्नमणिः कामेश्वरप्रेमरत्नमणिः; कामेश्वरप्रेमरत्नमणेः प्रतिपणौ कामेश्वरप्रेमरत्नमणिप्रतिपणौ; कामेश्वरप्रेमरत्नमणिप्रतिपणौ स्तनौ यस्याः सा कामेश्वरप्रेमरत्नमणिप्रतिपणस्तनी
samasa.vigraha_iast: kāmeśvarasya prema kāmeśvaraprema; ratnam maṇiḥ ratnamaṇiḥ; kāmeśvaraprema eva ratnamaṇiḥ kāmeśvarapremaratnamaṇiḥ; kāmeśvarapremaratnamaṇeḥ pratipaṇau kāmeśvarapremaratnamaṇipratipaṇau; kāmeśvarapremaratnamaṇipratipaṇau stanau yasyāḥ sā kāmeśvarapremaratnamaṇipratipaṇastanī
samasa.explanation: (1) kāmeśvara-prema 'Kāmeśvara's love' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (2) ratna-maṇi 'a precious gem' (karmadhāraya of two words for jewel), and (1) is identified with it: 'the precious gem that is Kāmeśvara's love' (rūpaka karmadhāraya). (3) …maṇi-pratipaṇa 'the counter-price for that gem', what is given in exchange for it (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (4) The whole is a bahuvrīhi: 'She whose breasts are the counter-price …'. stana 'breast', a body-part word ending the bahuvrīhi, takes the feminine ī (Pāṇini 4.1.54): -stanī.

components.note: appears as prema- in the compound (final n dropped)

components.meaning: counter-price, what is given in exchange

components.note: stana, with the feminine ī of the bahuvrīhi

names.meaning: She whose breasts are what She gives in return for the precious gem of Kāmeśvara's love
names.significance: Traditionally read as the perfect reciprocity of Śiva and Śakti: He gives His love, and She gives in return the nourishing fullness from which the worlds are sustained.

meaning_check.note: 'KAmeshvara' put into IAST and the wording brought closer to the compound (pratipaṇa, 'counter-price').

names.previous_split_issues: pratipaṇa was glossed 'given in exchange'; it is a noun, 'counter-price'. prema is the stem preman.

sandhi.rule: yaṇ: i becomes y before a dissimilar vowel (Pāṇini 6.1.77 iko yaṇ aci)
savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

samasa.type: bahuvrīhi (over inner rūpaka-karmadhārayas, a saptamī-tatpuruṣa and ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣas)
samasa.vigraha: नाभिः एव आलवालम् नाभ्यालवालम्; रोम्णाम् आलिः रोमालिः; रोमालिः एव लता रोमालिलता; नाभ्यालवाले रोमालिलता नाभ्यालवालरोमालिलता; नाभ्यालवालरोमालिलतायाः फलम् नाभ्यालवालरोमालिलताफलम्; कुचयोः द्वयी कुचद्वयी; नाभ्यालवालरोमालिलताफलम् कुचद्वयी यस्याः सा नाभ्यालवालरोमालिलताफलकुचद्वयी
samasa.vigraha_iast: nābhiḥ eva ālavālam nābhyālavālam; romṇām āliḥ romāliḥ; romāliḥ eva latā romālilatā; nābhyālavāle romālilatā nābhyālavālaromālilatā; nābhyālavālaromālilatāyāḥ phalam nābhyālavālaromālilatāphalam; kucayoḥ dvayī kucadvayī; nābhyālavālaromālilatāphalam kucadvayī yasyāḥ sā nābhyālavālaromālilatāphalakucadvayī
samasa.explanation: A sustained metaphor. (1) nābhi-ālavāla 'the navel as the water-basin at the foot of a plant' (rūpaka karmadhāraya). (2) roma-āli 'the line of fine hair' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa), itself (3) the creeper, latā (rūpaka). (4) The creeper is rooted in the navel-basin (saptamī-tatpuruṣa). (5) …latā-phala 'its fruit' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (6) kuca-dvayī 'the pair of breasts' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (7) The whole is a bahuvrīhi: 'She whose pair of breasts is the fruit of the hair-line creeper that grows from the navel-basin'.

components.meaning: basin of water at the foot of a tree or plant

components.note: appears as roma- in the compound (final n dropped)

names.meaning: She whose two breasts are the fruits of the creeper of fine hair that rises from the basin of Her navel
names.significance: A classical figure of Sanskrit poetry, carried through every member: the navel is the basin that waters the plant, the fine line of hair the creeper rising from it, and the breasts its fruit.

meaning_check.note: ālavāla is the water-basin at the root of a plant, not 'the depths'; the wording follows the compound's sustained metaphor.

names.previous_split_issues: nābhyālavāla was left as one row (nābhi 'navel' + ālavāla 'water-basin at a plant's foot'); romāli is roman + āli.

sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: ā + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ); the second member is ādhāratā 'being the support', not dhāratā — the fused ā hides the boundary
nasal assimilation: the d of the prefix ud becomes n before the nasal n (Pāṇini 8.4.45 yaro 'nunāsike 'nunāsiko vā)

samasa.type: bahuvrīhi (over an inner tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa, ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣas and a karmadhāraya)
samasa.vigraha: रोम्णाम् लता रोमलता; लक्ष्या रोमलता लक्ष्यरोमलता; लक्ष्यरोमलतायाः आधारता लक्ष्यरोमलताधारता; लक्ष्यरोमलताधारतया समुन्नेयम् लक्ष्यरोमलताधारतासमुन्नेयम्; लक्ष्यरोमलताधारतासमुन्नेयम् मध्यमम् यस्याः सा लक्ष्यरोमलताधारतासमुन्नेयमध्यमा
samasa.vigraha_iast: romṇām latā romalatā; lakṣyā romalatā lakṣyaromalatā; lakṣyaromalatāyāḥ ādhāratā lakṣyaromalatādhāratā; lakṣyaromalatādhāratayā samunneyam lakṣyaromalatādhāratāsamunneyam; lakṣyaromalatādhāratāsamunneyam madhyamam yasyāḥ sā lakṣyaromalatādhāratāsamunneyamadhyamā
samasa.explanation: (1) roma-latā 'the creeper of fine hair' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa, with the creeper metaphor of name 34), qualified by lakṣya 'visible' (karmadhāraya; lakṣyā takes its masculine stem, Pāṇini 6.3.42). (2) …latā-ādhāratā 'the fact of being the support of that creeper' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa; ādhāra + the abstract suffix -tā). (3) samunneya 'to be inferred' takes that fact in the instrumental, as the ground of the inference (tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa). (4) The whole is a bahuvrīhi: 'She whose waist (madhyama) is to be inferred from its being the support of the visible hair-creeper'.

components.note: appears as roma- in the compound

components.meaning: the being a support, the fact of bearing

components.note: sam + ud + √nī 'to lead', gerundive: lit. 'to be brought up (to the mind)'
madhyama, with the feminine -ā of the bahuvrīhi

names.meaning: She whose waist can be known only by inference, from its being the support of the visible creeper of fine hair
names.significance: Her waist is so slender that it is not seen; it is inferred because the visible line of hair must rest on something. Traditionally this is compared to the Supreme, which is not perceived directly but known from the world it upholds.

meaning_check.note: The compound says the waist is inferred from its being the support (ādhāratā) of the visible hair-creeper; the hair does not 'spring from' it.

names.previous_split_issues: The boundary was misplaced: latā + 'dhāratā' (glossed 'stream'). The member is ādhāratā 'being the support', whose initial ā merged with latā. lakṣya was glossed 'barely visible'; it means 'visible'.

sandhi.rule: nasal assimilation: the final t of the participle dalat becomes n before the nasal m (Pāṇini 8.4.45 yaro 'nunāsike 'nunāsiko vā)

samasa.type: bahuvrīhi (over inner tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa, karmadhārayas and ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣas)
samasa.vigraha: स्तनयोः भारः स्तनभारः; स्तनभारेण दलत् स्तनभारदलत्; स्तनभारदलत् मध्यम् स्तनभारदलन्मध्यम्; पट्टस्य बन्धः पट्टबन्धः; स्तनभारदलन्मध्यस्य पट्टबन्धः स्तनभारदलन्मध्यपट्टबन्धः; वलीनाम् त्रयम् वलित्रयम्; स्तनभारदलन्मध्यपट्टबन्धरूपम् वलित्रयम् यस्याः सा स्तनभारदलन्मध्यपट्टबन्धवलित्रया
samasa.vigraha_iast: stanayoḥ bhāraḥ stanabhāraḥ; stanabhāreṇa dalat stanabhāradalat; stanabhāradalat madhyam stanabhāradalanmadhyam; paṭṭasya bandhaḥ paṭṭabandhaḥ; stanabhāradalanmadhyasya paṭṭabandhaḥ stanabhāradalanmadhyapaṭṭabandhaḥ; valīnām trayam valitrayam; stanabhāradalanmadhyapaṭṭabandharūpam valitrayam yasyāḥ sā stanabhāradalanmadhyapaṭṭabandhavalitrayā
samasa.explanation: (1) stana-bhāra 'the weight of the breasts' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (2) The present participle dalat 'splitting, cracking' takes that weight in the instrumental (tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa), and (3) qualifies madhya 'waist' (karmadhāraya): 'the waist that seems to crack under the weight'. (4) paṭṭa-bandha 'a binding band' for that waist (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣas). (5) vali-traya 'the three folds' is identified with that band, the word 'in the form of' (rūpa) understood. (6) The whole is a bahuvrīhi: 'She whose three folds are a binding band for Her waist …'; traya takes the feminine -ā.

components.note: traya, with the feminine -ā of the bahuvrīhi

names.meaning: She whose three folds of skin form a band that binds Her waist, as though it would break under the weight of Her breasts
names.significance: The trivalī, three folds across the midriff, is a classical mark of beauty; the poet imagines them as a band tied by nature round a waist too slender for its burden.

meaning_check.note: Reworded to follow the compound: the three folds are themselves the binding band for the waist.

names.previous_split_issues: dalan was glossed 'bending'; it is the participle dalat 'splitting, cracking', its t nasalised before madhya. paṭṭa was glossed 'silk'; here it is a band. valitrayā was left as one row (vali + trayā).

sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

samasa.type: bahuvrīhi (over inner tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa, karmadhārayas and a ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa)
samasa.vigraha: अरुणः इव अरुणम् अरुणारुणम्; कौसुम्भम् वस्त्रम् कौसुम्भवस्त्रम्; अरुणारुणम् कौसुम्भवस्त्रम् अरुणारुणकौसुम्भवस्त्रम्; अरुणारुणकौसुम्भवस्त्रेण भास्वती अरुणारुणकौसुम्भवस्त्रभास्वती; कट्याः तटी कटीतटी; अरुणारुणकौसुम्भवस्त्रभास्वती कटीतटी यस्याः सा अरुणारुणकौसुम्भवस्त्रभास्वत्कटीतटी
samasa.vigraha_iast: aruṇaḥ iva aruṇam aruṇāruṇam; kausumbham vastram kausumbhavastram; aruṇāruṇam kausumbhavastram aruṇāruṇakausumbhavastram; aruṇāruṇakausumbhavastreṇa bhāsvatī aruṇāruṇakausumbhavastrabhāsvatī; kaṭyāḥ taṭī kaṭītaṭī; aruṇāruṇakausumbhavastrabhāsvatī kaṭītaṭī yasyāḥ sā aruṇāruṇakausumbhavastrabhāsvatkaṭītaṭī
samasa.explanation: (1) aruṇa-aruṇa: 'red like Aruṇa, the dawn' (upamāna-karmadhāraya, the standard of comparison compounded with the shared quality). (2) It qualifies kausumbha-vastra 'a safflower-dyed garment' (karmadhāraya). (3) bhāsvat 'shining' takes the garment in the instrumental (tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa). (4) kaṭī-taṭī 'the slope of the hips' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (5) The whole is a bahuvrīhi: 'She whose hips shine with a safflower-dyed garment red as the dawn'; bhāsvatī takes its masculine stem bhāsvat (puṃvadbhāva).

names.meaning: She whose hips shine with a safflower-dyed garment as red as the dawn
names.significance: Red is Her color throughout the hymn; its dhyāna verses picture Her as aruṇā, red, and in red garlands, ornaments and garments (aruṇa-mālya-bhūṣāmbarām). Traditionally the red is read as compassion and the passion (rāga) of creative power.

meaning_check.note: Shortened to the compound's own relations (bhāsvat 'shining with'); the safflower is in kausumbha, not a separate 'extract'.

names.previous_split_issues: aruṇāruṇa was left as one row (aruṇa + aruṇa). kausumbha was glossed 'saffron-dyed'; it is dyed with safflower (kusumbha), not saffron (kuṅkuma).
names.uncertain: aruṇāruṇa may be read as 'red as the dawn' (upamāna, as analysed) or as the color word doubled for emphasis, 'deep red, red upon red'.

samasa.type: tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa (over inner karmadhārayas, a tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa and a ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa)
samasa.vigraha: रत्नमय्यः किङ्किणिकाः रत्नकिङ्किणिकाः; रत्नकिङ्किणिकाभिः रम्यम् रत्नकिङ्किणिकारम्यम्; रशनायाः दाम रशनादाम; रत्नकिङ्किणिकारम्यम् रशनादाम रत्नकिङ्किणिकारम्यरशनादाम; तेन भूषिता रत्नकिङ्किणिकारम्यरशनादामभूषिता
samasa.vigraha_iast: ratnamayyaḥ kiṅkiṇikāḥ ratnakiṅkiṇikāḥ; ratnakiṅkiṇikābhiḥ ramyam ratnakiṅkiṇikāramyam; raśanāyāḥ dāma raśanādāma; ratnakiṅkiṇikāramyam raśanādāma ratnakiṅkiṇikāramyaraśanādāma; tena bhūṣitā ratnakiṅkiṇikāramyaraśanādāmabhūṣitā
samasa.explanation: (1) ratna-kiṅkiṇikā 'little bells made of gems' (karmadhāraya with 'made of' understood). (2) ramya 'lovely' takes them in the instrumental (tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa). (3) raśanā-dāma 'the chain or string of the girdle' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa), qualified by (2) (karmadhāraya). (4) The participle bhūṣitā 'adorned' is the head and takes the girdle-chain in the instrumental.

components.note: appears as dāma- in the compound (final n dropped)

names.meaning: She who is adorned with a girdle-chain made lovely by little jewelled bells
names.significance: The girdle with small bells (kiṅkiṇī) is a classical ornament of the hips; its sound is part of the poetic picture of Her presence.

meaning_check.note: 'decorated with many … bells' tightened to the compound: ramya 'made lovely' by the bells, and dāma 'chain, string' of the girdle.

names.previous_split_issues: dāma is the stem dāman 'string, chain', not 'garland' here.

sandhi.rule: guṇa: a + ī → e (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ), inside the lexicalised name Kāmeśa
guṇa: a + ū → o (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ)
savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)
yaṇ: u becomes v before a dissimilar vowel (Pāṇini 6.1.77 iko yaṇ aci), at the junction of the prefix anu with ita

samasa.type: tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa (over inner bahuvrīhi, dvandva, tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa, karmadhāraya and ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa)
samasa.vigraha: सौभाग्यम् च मार्दवम् च सौभाग्यमार्दवे; कामेशेन ज्ञाते कामेशज्ञाते; कामेशज्ञाते सौभाग्यमार्दवे ययोः तौ कामेशज्ञातसौभाग्यमार्दवौ; कामेशज्ञातसौभाग्यमार्दवौ ऊरू कामेशज्ञातसौभाग्यमार्दवोरू; तयोः द्वयम् कामेशज्ञातसौभाग्यमार्दवोरुद्वयम्; तेन अन्विता कामेशज्ञातसौभाग्यमार्दवोरुद्वयान्विता
samasa.vigraha_iast: saubhāgyam ca mārdavam ca saubhāgyamārdave; kāmeśena jñāte kāmeśajñāte; kāmeśajñāte saubhāgyamārdave yayoḥ tau kāmeśajñātasaubhāgyamārdavau; kāmeśajñātasaubhāgyamārdavau ūrū kāmeśajñātasaubhāgyamārdavorū; tayoḥ dvayam kāmeśajñātasaubhāgyamārdavorudvayam; tena anvitā kāmeśajñātasaubhāgyamārdavorudvayānvitā
samasa.explanation: (1) saubhāgya-mārdava 'beauty and softness' (dvandva). (2) kāmeśa-jñāta 'known by Kāmeśa' (tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa) qualifies them. (3) Together they form a bahuvrīhi describing the thighs: 'whose beauty and softness are known to Kāmeśa', qualifying ūru 'thigh' (karmadhāraya). (4) …ūru-dvaya 'the pair of such thighs' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (5) anvitā 'endowed with' is the head and takes the pair in the instrumental. 'Only' is not a word in the name; it is the traditional sense of 'known by Kāmeśa'.

names.meaning: She whose two thighs, in their beauty and softness, are known to Kāmeśa alone
names.significance: Traditionally read as the intimacy of Śiva and Śakti: what She is in full is known only to Kāmeśvara, who is Her own Self.

meaning_check.note: Rephrased to begin 'She …'; 'kAmesha' put into IAST.

names.previous_split_issues: mārdavoru was left as one row (mārdava + ūru, joined by guṇa); dvayānvitā was left as one row (dvaya + anvitā).

sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

samasa.type: tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa (over an inner karmadhāraya, a bahuvrīhi of resemblance and a ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa)
samasa.vigraha: माणिक्यमयः मुकुटः माणिक्यमुकुटः; माणिक्यमुकुटस्य आकारः इव आकारः यस्य तत् माणिक्यमुकुटाकारम्; जान्वोः द्वयम् जानुद्वयम्; माणिक्यमुकुटाकारम् जानुद्वयम् माणिक्यमुकुटाकारजानुद्वयम्; तेन विराजिता माणिक्यमुकुटाकारजानुद्वयविराजिता
samasa.vigraha_iast: māṇikyamayaḥ mukuṭaḥ māṇikyamukuṭaḥ; māṇikyamukuṭasya ākāraḥ iva ākāraḥ yasya tat māṇikyamukuṭākāram; jānvoḥ dvayam jānudvayam; māṇikyamukuṭākāram jānudvayam māṇikyamukuṭākārajānudvayam; tena virājitā māṇikyamukuṭākārajānudvayavirājitā
samasa.explanation: (1) māṇikya-mukuṭa 'a crown of ruby' (karmadhāraya with 'made of' understood). (2) …mukuṭa-ākāra 'having the shape of such a crown' (bahuvrīhi of resemblance, as in name 25). (3) It qualifies jānu-dvaya 'the pair of knees' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa inside; karmadhāraya). (4) virājitā 'shining' is the head and takes the knees in the instrumental.

names.meaning: She who shines with two knees shaped like crowns of ruby
names.significance: The rounded, glowing kneecaps are likened to small domed crowns of ruby; the red of the ruby again answers to Her color.

meaning_check.note: Rephrased to follow the compound (virājitā 'shining with'); ITRANS 'mAnikya' removed.

names.previous_split_issues: makuṭākāra was left as one row; it is mukuṭa 'crown' + ākāra 'shape' (the spelling of the stem was corrected to mukuṭa in the text).
names.variants: Many printed editions read माणिक्यमकुटाकार (makuṭa). makuṭa is a recognized by-form of mukuṭa 'crown' in the lexicons, so that reading is a variant spelling rather than a misprint; the sense is the same.

sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

samasa.type: bahuvrīhi (over an inner bahuvrīhi of resemblance, a karmadhāraya, a tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa and a ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa)
samasa.vigraha: इन्द्रगोपैः परिक्षिप्तः इन्द्रगोपपरिक्षिप्तः; स्मरस्य तूणः स्मरतूणः; इन्द्रगोपपरिक्षिप्तः स्मरतूणः इन्द्रगोपपरिक्षिप्तस्मरतूणः; इन्द्रगोपपरिक्षिप्तस्मरतूणस्य आभा इव आभा ययोः ते इन्द्रगोपपरिक्षिप्तस्मरतूणाभे; इन्द्रगोपपरिक्षिप्तस्मरतूणाभे जङ्घिके यस्याः सा इन्द्रगोपपरिक्षिप्तस्मरतूणाभजङ्घिका
samasa.vigraha_iast: indragopaiḥ parikṣiptaḥ indragopaparikṣiptaḥ; smarasya tūṇaḥ smaratūṇaḥ; indragopaparikṣiptaḥ smaratūṇaḥ indragopaparikṣiptasmaratūṇaḥ; indragopaparikṣiptasmaratūṇasya ābhā iva ābhā yayoḥ te indragopaparikṣiptasmaratūṇābhe; indragopaparikṣiptasmaratūṇābhe jaṅghike yasyāḥ sā indragopaparikṣiptasmaratūṇābhajaṅghikā
samasa.explanation: (1) indragopa-parikṣipta 'set all around with indragopas' (tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa). (2) smara-tūṇa 'the quiver of Smara (Kāma)' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa), qualified by (1) (karmadhāraya). (3) …tūṇa-ābha 'having the look of that quiver' (bahuvrīhi of resemblance). (4) The whole is a bahuvrīhi: 'She whose calves (jaṅghikā) look like Kāma's quiver set around with indragopas'. The tapering, rounded calf is the quiver.

components.meaning: indragopa, a small scarlet velvet insect that appears in the rains
components.note: lit. 'Indra's cowherd'; one word, not Indra + 'beetle'

components.meaning: Smara, Kāma, the god of love

components.note: ābhā 'light, look', at the end of a compound

names.meaning: She whose calves resemble the quiver of Kāma, studded all around with scarlet indragopas
names.significance: The comparison is to Kāma's quiver, which holds the flower-arrows; in this hymn those arrows are Her own (name 11). The scarlet indragopas, like the ruby knees of name 40, keep the description in Her color, red.

meaning_check.note: 'jewel-covered' replaced by what the name says: set around with indragopas, scarlet insects (or red gems of their hue); 'God of Love' given as Kāma.

names.previous_split_issues: indragopa was split into 'Indra' + 'beetle'. It is one word, the name of a scarlet insect; gopa alone does not mean beetle. tūṇābha was left as one row (tūṇa + ābha).
names.uncertain: Translators take indragopa here either as the scarlet insects themselves, scattered over the quiver, or as red gems of their color set around it; the comparison of the calves to Kāma's quiver is not in doubt.

samasa.type: bahuvrīhi
samasa.vigraha: गूढौ गुल्फौ यस्याः सा गूढगुल्फा
samasa.vigraha_iast: gūḍhau gulphau yasyāḥ sā gūḍhagulphā
samasa.explanation: gūḍha 'hidden' qualifies gulpha 'ankle'; the compound describes Her: 'She whose ankles are hidden'. gulpha takes the feminine -ā. The members are simply juxtaposed.

components.note: gulpha, with the feminine -ā of the bahuvrīhi

names.meaning: She whose ankles are hidden
names.significance: Ankles that are full and rounded, with the bone not standing out, are a classical mark of beauty in the description of the body.

sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)
yaṇ: u becomes v before a dissimilar vowel (Pāṇini 6.1.77 iko yaṇ aci), at the junction of the prefix anu with ita

samasa.type: tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa (over an inner karmadhāraya, a tatpuruṣa of object and agent-adjective, and a ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa)
samasa.vigraha: कूर्मस्य पृष्ठम् कूर्मपृष्ठम्; कूर्मपृष्ठम् जयिष्णुनी कूर्मपृष्ठजयिष्णुनी; कूर्मपृष्ठजयिष्णुनी प्रपदे कूर्मपृष्ठजयिष्णुप्रपदे; ताभ्याम् अन्विता कूर्मपृष्ठजयिष्णुप्रपदान्विता
samasa.vigraha_iast: kūrmasya pṛṣṭham kūrmapṛṣṭham; kūrmapṛṣṭham jayiṣṇunī kūrmapṛṣṭhajayiṣṇunī; kūrmapṛṣṭhajayiṣṇunī prapade kūrmapṛṣṭhajayiṣṇuprapade; tābhyām anvitā kūrmapṛṣṭhajayiṣṇuprapadānvitā
samasa.explanation: (1) kūrma-pṛṣṭha 'the back of a tortoise' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (2) jayiṣṇu 'surpassing, victorious over' takes it as its object (a tatpuruṣa of object and agent-adjective). (3) It qualifies prapada 'instep, forefoot' (karmadhāraya). (4) The participle anvitā 'endowed with' is the head and takes the insteps in the instrumental.

components.meaning: instep, the forepart of the foot

names.meaning: She whose insteps surpass the back of a tortoise in their smooth curve
names.significance: A high, smoothly arched instep, like a tortoise's shell, is a classical mark of beauty in the description of the feet.

meaning_check.note: Typo 'smooothness' removed; prapada is the instep (forefoot), and the compound says it surpasses the tortoise's back.

names.previous_split_issues: prapadānvitā was left as one row (prapada + anvitā); prapada was glossed 'forefoot' but the meaning spoke of 'arches'.

sandhi.rule: the m of the prefix sam becomes anusvāra and then the palatal nasal ñ before ch (Pāṇini 8.3.23 mo 'nusvāraḥ; 8.4.58 anusvārasya yayi parasavarṇaḥ); written here with ñ, elsewhere as saṃchanna
the final t of the participle namat is voiced to d (jaśtva, Pāṇini 8.2.39) and assimilated to the following palatal j (ścutva, Pāṇini 8.4.40 stoḥ ścunā ścuḥ)
the final s becomes ru (Pāṇini 8.2.66 sasajuṣo ruḥ), which turns to u after a before a voiced consonant (6.1.114 haśi ca); a + u then gives o by guṇa (6.1.87)

samasa.type: bahuvrīhi (over inner tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa, karmadhārayas and ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣas)
samasa.vigraha: नखानाम् दीधितयः नखदीधितयः; नखदीधितिभिः सञ्छन्नः नखदीधितिसञ्छन्नः; नमन्तः जनाः नमज्जनाः; तमः गुणः तमोगुणः; नमज्जनानाम् तमोगुणः नमज्जनतमोगुणः; नखदीधितिसञ्छन्नः नमज्जनतमोगुणः यस्याः सा नखदीधितिसञ्छन्ननमज्जनतमोगुणा
samasa.vigraha_iast: nakhānām dīdhitayaḥ nakhadīdhitayaḥ; nakhadīdhitibhiḥ sañchannaḥ nakhadīdhitisañchannaḥ; namantaḥ janāḥ namajjanāḥ; tamaḥ guṇaḥ tamoguṇaḥ; namajjanānām tamoguṇaḥ namajjanatamoguṇaḥ; nakhadīdhitisañchannaḥ namajjanatamoguṇaḥ yasyāḥ sā nakhadīdhitisañchannanamajjanatamoguṇā
samasa.explanation: (1) nakha-dīdhiti 'the rays of the (toe)nails' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (2) sañchanna 'covered over, overwhelmed' takes the rays in the instrumental (tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa). (3) namaj-jana 'people who bow' (karmadhāraya of participle and noun). (4) tamo-guṇa 'the guṇa tamas', darkness, inertia, ignorance (karmadhāraya), and …jana-tamoguṇa 'the tamas of those who bow' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (5) The whole is a bahuvrīhi: 'She by the rays of whose toenails the tamas of those who bow is covered over', i.e. overwhelmed and dispelled by light; guṇa takes the feminine -ā.

components.meaning: darkness; tamas, the guṇa of inertia and ignorance

components.note: guṇa, with the feminine -ā of the bahuvrīhi

names.meaning: She the radiance of whose toenails overwhelms the darkness (tamoguṇa) of those who bow to Her
names.significance: Those who bow touch Her feet with their heads, and the light of Her toenails falls on them. Traditionally this is the removal of ignorance through surrender at Her feet.

meaning_check.note: Brought closer to the compound: the rays 'cover over' (sañchanna) the tamas of those who bow; 'dispelled' is the sense, not the word.

names.previous_split_issues: The spelling saṃchanna was updated to sañchanna. namajjana was left as one row (namat 'bowing' + jana 'people'); 'tamo' was given in its sandhi form (the stem is tamas); guṇā was glossed 'quality of'.

sandhi.rule: the final s becomes ru (Pāṇini 8.2.66), which turns to u after a before the voiced r (6.1.114 haśi ca); a + u gives o by guṇa (6.1.87), inside the lexicalised word saroruha 'lotus'

samasa.type: bahuvrīhi (over an inner tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa and ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣas)
samasa.vigraha: पदयोः द्वयम् पदद्वयम्; पदद्वयस्य प्रभा पदद्वयप्रभा; पदद्वयप्रभायाः जालम् पदद्वयप्रभाजालम्; पदद्वयप्रभाजालेन पराकृतानि पदद्वयप्रभाजालपराकृतानि; पदद्वयप्रभाजालपराकृतानि सरोरुहाणि यस्याः सा पदद्वयप्रभाजालपराकृतसरोरुहा
samasa.vigraha_iast: padayoḥ dvayam padadvayam; padadvayasya prabhā padadvayaprabhā; padadvayaprabhāyāḥ jālam padadvayaprabhājālam; padadvayaprabhājālena parākṛtāni padadvayaprabhājālaparākṛtāni; padadvayaprabhājālaparākṛtāni saroruhāṇi yasyāḥ sā padadvayaprabhājālaparākṛtasaroruhā
samasa.explanation: (1) pada-dvaya 'the two feet', …dvaya-prabhā 'their radiance', …prabhā-jāla 'the mass (lit. net) of that radiance' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣas). (2) The passive participle parākṛta 'defeated, set aside' takes it in the instrumental (tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa). (3) It qualifies saroruha 'lotus' and the whole is a bahuvrīhi: 'She by the radiance of whose two feet the lotuses are put to shame'; saroruha takes the feminine -ā.

components.meaning: defeated, set aside, put to shame

components.note: saroruha 'growing in a lake' (saras 'lake' + ruha 'growing'), with the feminine -ā of the bahuvrīhi

names.meaning: She whose two feet, by their mass of radiance, put the lotuses to shame
names.significance: The lotus is the usual image for the feet of the deity; here the feet outshine the very flower they are compared to.

meaning_check.note: jāla 'mass of radiance' and the dual 'two feet' kept; the lotuses are 'put to shame', not merely 'defeated in radiance'.

names.previous_split_issues: saroruhā was glossed 'lotus' without its parts (saras + ruha); parākṛta was glossed 'excelling' — it is passive, 'defeated, set aside'.

sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

samasa.type: bahuvrīhi (over inner karmadhārayas, a rūpaka and a tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa)
samasa.vigraha: मणिमयाः मञ्जीराः मणिमञ्जीराः; शिञ्जानाः मणिमञ्जीराः शिञ्जानमणिमञ्जीराः; शिञ्जानमणिमञ्जीरैः मण्डिते शिञ्जानमणिमञ्जीरमण्डिते; पदे एव अम्बुजे पदाम्बुजे; श्रीमती पदाम्बुजे श्रीपदाम्बुजे; शिञ्जानमणिमञ्जीरमण्डिते श्रीपदाम्बुजे यस्याः सा शिञ्जानमणिमञ्जीरमण्डितश्रीपदाम्बुजा
samasa.vigraha_iast: maṇimayāḥ mañjīrāḥ maṇimañjīrāḥ; śiñjānāḥ maṇimañjīrāḥ śiñjānamaṇimañjīrāḥ; śiñjānamaṇimañjīraiḥ maṇḍite śiñjānamaṇimañjīramaṇḍite; pade eva ambuje padāmbuje; śrīmatī padāmbuje śrīpadāmbuje; śiñjānamaṇimañjīramaṇḍite śrīpadāmbuje yasyāḥ sā śiñjānamaṇimañjīramaṇḍitaśrīpadāmbujā
samasa.explanation: (1) maṇi-mañjīra 'jewelled anklets' (karmadhāraya with 'made of' understood), qualified by the participle śiñjāna 'tinkling' (karmadhāraya). (2) maṇḍita 'adorned' takes the anklets in the instrumental (tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa). (3) pada-ambuja 'the feet that are lotuses' (rūpaka karmadhāraya), with the honorific śrī 'auspicious, glorious'. (4) The whole is a bahuvrīhi: 'She whose auspicious lotus-feet are adorned with tinkling jewelled anklets'; ambuja takes the feminine -ā.

components.note: √śiñj 'to tinkle' (Dhātupāṭha śiji avyakte śabde), present participle (middle)
ambuja 'water-born' (ambu + ja), with the feminine -ā of the bahuvrīhi

names.meaning: She whose auspicious lotus feet are adorned with tinkling jewelled anklets
names.significance: With the feet the description of Her form, begun with the hair at name 13, is complete. In Śrīvidyā Her feet (pādukā) are the highest object of worship and the refuge of the devotee.

meaning_check.note: 'golden' and 'sweetly' are not in the name and were removed.

names.previous_split_issues: mañjira was spelled with a short i (mañjīra, long ī, is the word); padāmbujā was left as one row (pada + ambuja).
names.variants: Some printings spell the participle with dental s: सिञ्जान (siñjāna). √śiñj is the Dhātupāṭha form; siñj is recorded in the lexicons as a by-spelling.

samasa.type: bahuvrīhi (over an inner upamāna-karmadhāraya)
samasa.vigraha: मराली इव मन्दम् मरालीमन्दम्; मरालीमन्दम् गमनम् यस्याः सा मरालीमन्दगमना
samasa.vigraha_iast: marālī iva mandam marālīmandam; marālīmandam gamanam yasyāḥ sā marālīmandagamanā
samasa.explanation: (1) marālī-manda 'slow like a female swan': the standard of comparison compounded with the shared quality (upamāna-karmadhāraya, as in name 15). (2) It qualifies gamana 'gait', and the whole is a bahuvrīhi describing Her; gamana takes the feminine -ā. The members are simply juxtaposed.

components.note: gamana from √gam 'to go', with the feminine -ā of the bahuvrīhi

names.meaning: She whose gait is as slow and gentle as that of a swan
names.significance: The unhurried, gliding gait of the swan is the classical image of graceful, stately movement.
names.previous_split_issues: marālī was glossed 'swan-like'; it is 'female swan', and the likeness comes from the compound.

samasa.type: ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa (with an inner karmadhāraya)
samasa.vigraha: महत् लावण्यम् महालावण्यम्; महालावण्यस्य शेवधिः महालावण्यशेवधिः
samasa.vigraha_iast: mahat lāvaṇyam mahālāvaṇyam; mahālāvaṇyasya śevadhiḥ mahālāvaṇyaśevadhiḥ
samasa.explanation: (1) mahā-lāvaṇya 'great beauty' (karmadhāraya; mahat becomes mahā- before a co-referential member, Pāṇini 6.3.46). (2) śevadhi 'treasure, treasury' is the head and the beauty stands to it in the genitive. As a tatpuruṣa it keeps the head's masculine gender (2.4.26), so the name ends -śevadhiḥ, not with a feminine ending, though it names the Goddess.

components.note: appears as mahā- in a karmadhāraya (Pāṇini 6.3.46)
abstract noun from lavaṇa, lit. 'saltiness', hence piquancy, charm

names.meaning: She who is the treasure-house of supreme beauty
names.significance: The name sums up the description of Her form that ends here: all beauty is stored in Her, and every lesser loveliness is drawn from that treasury.

meaning_check.note: mahā 'great, supreme' had not been translated.

verse_notes.note: Name 27: kacchapī is the vīṇā of Sarasvatī, not a tortoise. Name 28: majjat 'sinking' is intransitive; Kāmeśa's mind sinks in the flood of Her smile.
Kāmeśa (28, 30, 39) is kāma + īśa joined by guṇa; the name cannot be hyphenated across the e.
Name 32: divide muktāphala-anvitā; phala belongs to muktāphala 'pearl', and anvitā 'endowed with' governs all three ornaments.
Name 34 begins nābhi + ālavāla (yaṇ); its metaphor of basin, creeper and fruit continues into name 35.
Name 35: divide latā + ādhāratā 'being the support', not latā + dhāratā; the ā of ādhāratā is fused with latā. Name 36: dalan- is the participle dalat, its t nasalised before madhya.
Name 37: kausumbha is dyed with safflower (kusumbha), not saffron.
Name 39: mārdavoru is mārdava + ūru 'thigh'. Name 40: many editions spell makuṭa, a by-form of mukuṭa 'crown'.
Name 41: indragopa is one word, a scarlet insect (not Indra + 'beetle'). The second half holds two names: gūḍhagulphā (42) | kūrmapṛṣṭha… (43).
tamoguṇa (44) and saroruha (45) both show s → o: tamas + guṇa, saras + ruha.

With name 46 the head-to-foot description begun at name 13 reaches the feet; 47–48 sum up Her gait and beauty. The second half holds two names: marālīmandagamanā (47) | mahālāvaṇyaśevadhiḥ (48), which keeps the masculine of its head śevadhi.

report.summary: Checked all 22 names of ślokas 11–20 against text.json: sandhi at every member junction (including prefix junctions sam + lāpa, ud + neya, sam + channa), a layered samāsa analysis with pausa-form vigraha-vākyas, and the meanings against that analysis. Two members were misidentified in the old split (35: ādhāratā 'being the support', not dhāratā 'stream'; 41: indragopa is one word, a scarlet insect, not Indra + 'beetle') and one member boundary was wrong (32: phala belongs to muktāphala 'pearl'); name 32's meaning was replaced. No error was found in the Sanskrit; name 40's recent correction to mukuṭa is sound, but the earlier makuṭa is a recognized by-form and is recorded as a variant, not a typo. No external sandhi joins names in these ślokas.
